definition: Stochastic hill climbing is a variant of the basic hill climbing method.
details: While basic hill climbing always chooses the steepest uphill move, "stochastic hill climbing chooses at random from among the uphill moves; the probability of selection can vary with the steepness of the uphill move."

explainer.lead: A hill-climbing variant that picks randomly among uphill moves instead of always taking the steepest one. It matters because randomness can help search escape the traps that strict steepest-ascent falls into.

tiers.eli5: Instead of always taking the biggest step up the hill, you pick any step that goes up, chosen at random — bigger gains can still be more likely to be picked.
tiers.practitioner: Used for cheap local search where you want diversity in the moves; a common pitfall is that unguided randomness slows convergence unless selection probability is tied to steepness.
tiers.paperLevel: Each iteration: among all neighbouring moves that improve the objective, select one at random, with selection probability possibly varying with the steepness of the uphill move. No guarantee of reaching the global optimum.

explainer.example: From a node with three improving neighbours of gains 3, 2, and 1, a stochastic hill climber might pick the gain-2 move rather than the steepest gain-3 move.
